title: First time showing what I have accomplished so far - The Trials of the Forsaken Knight
author: ClownLogicGames
selftext:
I have had a blast learning how to use various AI tools and manual editing to create what will be my first published game.  I am looking for any positive/negative feedback, thoughts, and questions on what I have so far to make this is appealing (and fun) as possible.  I just launched [Steam Page](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4712170/) yesterday.  The mechanics and core loop are in a great shape so now I am focusing on adding more content (I have 32 fights so far of a planned 98).

Hopefully this is clear from the trailer/steam page, but the gist is that this is a fighting game focused on proper timing of attacks and parries and adapting to the various attack patterns/fighting styles of different enemies - originally inspired by the rather simple NES Punch-Out combat, but gradually became more complex I went.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: so why do the battlers look like cartoons when everything else is in realistic style? your intro graphics and backgrounds are all in realistic style. not that the battlers look bad, I just thought the mix of the style seems odd

replies.author: ClownLogicGames
replies.body: Hmm, I hadn't expected this to be off-putting but that's why feedback matters.  I can experiment with a more cartoonish background / UI elements to see how that looks.  I like the appearance of the characters and it is also dramatically more realistic for me to animate with the simpler style, so bringing the other elements more in line with their style is probably the way to go.

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body:
Definitely bring the background in line with the art style, I would also suggest to improve the UI. It's taking up such a HUGE portion of the screen

https://preview.redd.it/fzqiejpl560h1.png?width=2550&format=png&auto=webp&s=65c2bd74cada28dab510ac9095eedaabb1987729

I think (without understanding what the letters/symbols are on the left) you could change those from bars to a radial element, like a circle around the symbol that fills up over time. I don't really know how the letter corresponds to each symbol, I feel as though you wouldn't need the letter if you already have something explaining what each symbol is in the game (whether it's done in the tutorial or something in the options menu like a context menu or something)

Maybe try experimenting with having the symbols across the bottom of the screen, and then you could move the health/stamina/power bars hard left and right respectively, then place the Cave/Duel part as a smaller asset in the center of the screen. I think this would just help it feel less cluttered personally, that's my take

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
Agreed on bringing the background inline with the art style.

I do like the idea of them using some type of radial along the bottom. or if they really want to keep up on the side, then radial there.

\---

My initial interpretation of the letters was what keyboard letter did what action and letting the player know the cooldown.

Q: Quaffs a healing potion and restore health. Longer cooldown.

W: Wait/rest to quickly recover Stamina. Longer cooldown.

E: Energizes self by calming up with shouting. Recover Power.

A: Attempt to parry. Parry seems to negate stamina loss if successful.

S: Standard attack. Short cooldown.

D: Delivers flaming slash, but longer animation and probably deals more damage. Probably uses up Power.

F: A slash that Fs up the enemy / knocks them the F out for a bit. Probably uses up Power.

And then if you lose all your Stamina (from attacking or getting hit), you get knocked down, can't do stuff recover your Stamina, lower your Power.

OP can correct me if I have an incorrect interpretation of their UI or trailer.

replies.author: ClownLogicGames
replies.body: This is very close, F is a stunning attack but otherwise you pretty much nailed every part of this!
